source.title: Tierkreis: A Dataflow Framework for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing

claims.text: We present Tierkreis, a higher-order dataflow graph program representation and runtime designed for compositional, quantum-classical hybrid algorithms.
claims.claim_text: We present Tierkreis, a higher-order dataflow graph program representation and runtime designed for compositional, quantum-classical hybrid algorithms.

claims.text: The design of the system is motivated by the remote nature of quantum computers, the need for hybrid algorithms to involve cloud and distributed computing, and the long-running nature of these algorithms.
claims.claim_text: The design of the system is motivated by the remote nature of quantum computers, the need for hybrid algorithms to involve cloud and distributed computing, and the long-running nature of these algorithms.

claims.text: The graph-based representation reflects how designers reason about and visualise algorithms, and allows automatic parallelism and asynchronicity.
claims.claim_text: The graph-based representation reflects how designers reason about and visualise algorithms, and allows automatic parallelism and asynchronicity.

claims.text: A strong, static type system and higherorder semantics allow for high expressivity and compositionality in the program.
claims.claim_text: A strong, static type system and higherorder semantics allow for high expressivity and compositionality in the program.

claims.text: The flexible runtime protocol enables thirdparty developers to add functionality using any language or environment.
claims.claim_text: The flexible runtime protocol enables thirdparty developers to add functionality using any language or environment.

claims.text: With Tierkreis, quantum software developers can easily build, visualise, verify, test, and debug complex hybrid workflows, and immediately deploy them to the cloud or a custom distributed environment.
